html:
Heydar Aliyev was the leader of Azerbaijan for most of three decades, born in 1923 in Nakhchivan, first as Soviet party boss and then as president from 1993 to 2003.

A career KGB officer, he headed the Azerbaijan Communist Party from 1969 to 1982 and then sat on the Politburo in Moscow, until Gorbachev pushed him out. He returned to his native Nakhchivan and in 1993, amid defeat in the Karabakh war and a military revolt, took power in Baku. He signed the 1994 ceasefire and the Contract of the Century with Western oil firms, and built a tightly controlled state. His son Ilham succeeded him in 2003, and his cult dominates Azerbaijan's public life.
